title: A combined change does not isolate each ingredient
paragraphs: Researchers delayed downbeats AND synchronized offbeats; listeners were over seven times as likely to hear swing in modified pieces.

D links timing to swing. A says offbeat synchronization works regardless of downbeats, an isolation the design does not establish. B invents difficulty of manipulation; C introduces absent piano/nonpiano comparison.
transfer: Mark every changed variable. If A and B changed together, improvement can support the package without proving A works alone.

title: Hold mass distinct from percentage
paragraphs: A coin has 74.2% silver, below an 80% trade threshold, while financial pressure persists.

B keeps silver amount constant while reducing total coin weight, increasing silver proportion by removing other material. A raises the acceptance hurdle; C retains the failing proportion despite heavier weight; D adds copper supply rather than solving composition.
transfer: Write proportion = part / whole. A fixed part can occupy a larger share when the whole shrinks.

title: A threshold can depend on competitors
paragraphs: Text1 model gives male reproductive advantage only when comparatively large enough to defend territory. Text2 removes males from one tank; 81% of females begin change there, none in the other.

B applies comparative size to each tank. A overstates that even small females benefit and adds a largest-females tank2 claim. C reverses advantage. D invokes population reproduction needs rather than requested individual size-advantage model.
transfer: Name the model’s criterion and apply it in both conditions. A plausible explanation still fails if it is not the requested model.

title: Keep possible causes separate across comparisons
paragraphs: Daughters match mothers for two years but not five; same-habitat unrelated bears show modest correlation; nonmaternal relatives are no more correlated than unrelated bears independent of habitat.

B retains diminishing social learning and possible environment. A misuses shared habitat to explain mother/daughter divergence; C discards learning; D adds significant genetics contrary to relative-control comparison.
transfer: Pair each candidate cause with its informative comparison. Some residual support does not establish that factor as the only driver.

title: Success can fail at the final stage
paragraphs: Low artificial night light did not significantly alter clownfish spawning or fertilization, but completely inhibited hatching.
B predicts reproductive risk if fish settle in lit regions. A contradicts unchanged fertilization. C compares absent other-species data. D invents ranking of two nonsignificant earlier-stage effects.
transfer: Keep the endpoint separate from intermediate measures. Successful early stages cannot rescue a blocked necessary later stage.

title: A false signal can still persuade
paragraphs: Carotenoids ordinarily produce saturated color and confer health benefits; some tanagers simulate saturation via feather microstructures without a carotenoid-rich diet.
D allows dishonest fitness signaling. A calls it honest despite decoupling. B claims lower effectiveness, although no mate response is measured. C changes issue to unexplained preference.
transfer: Ask separately whether a signal is true and whether its audience responds. Deception does not imply ineffective communication.

title: A null extra effect does not erase a large baseline effect
paragraphs: Ships alone and ships plus sonic pulses both reduce deep dives compared with natural sound; their effects differ negligibly.

B explains pulses adding little to already dominant ship sound. A predicts a difference rather than similarity. C contradicts negligible behavioral difference. D mistakes no incremental pulse effect for low overall sensitivity.
transfer: Use three columns: natural, A, A+B. Compare A to natural separately from A+B to A.

title: Two explanations can imply the same conclusion
paragraphs: Shared leaf/root bacteria may come from soil splashed upward OR from wind depositing onto leaves and soil.
B common source follows under either account. A/D invent benefit/harm. C is compatible with one account but not established by both.
transfer: When a prompt says either explanation, find a consequence invariant across the alternatives; do not choose one explanation.

title: A broader population does not broaden everything measured
paragraphs: Participants from 53 countries supplied personality and preference data, but the assessed music genres were Western.
A supports cross-cultural personality/preference association for Western music. B extends to untested non-Western styles. C invents previous expectations; D invents familiarity comparisons.
transfer: Track population scope separately from stimulus or outcome scope. Global participants can still answer a question about one class of music.

title: An event date is different from how long it takes
paragraphs: Text1 proposes moon formation over thousands of years; detailed Text2 simulation suggests a few hours after impact.
D identifies formation speed disagreement. A changes the calendar timing of formation, which neither text provides. B/C introduce Theia-evidence and surface-similarity comparisons.
transfer: Write when versus how long beside time claims before comparing texts.

title: Agree on the measurement while disputing its clock
paragraphs: Mo increases in a layer dated 2.5 Ga. One team dates oxygen increase to then; another proposes later weathering through microfractures.
B isolates disagreement about contemporaneous oxygen. C weathering mechanism is shared. D wrongly says measured Mo increase is false. A asks earlier oxygen conditions outside the dispute.
transfer: Separate measured amount, mechanism, and event time. An observation can be reliable while its interpretation as a date proxy fails.

title: A conclusion can survive replacement of its evidence
paragraphs: Initial shared chicken mutation proved globally widespread. New markers shared by South America and Polynesia but absent in European breeds support the same Polynesian-origin claim.
D agrees with conclusion while preferring stronger later evidence. A invents chronology conflict; B invents reverse-transfer objection; C invents European uniformity assumption.
transfer: Track stance toward the conclusion separately from stance toward the supporting evidence.

title: An old object is not automatically evidence of old humans
paragraphs: Old-layer stones are called tools in Text1; Text2 says natural fracturing remains plausible and corroborating human traces are absent.

B locates unsupported human-made-tool assumption. A invents connection between groups. C predicts eventual confirmation without support. D challenges Clovis date rather than relevant stone classification.
transfer: Identify the bridge from observation to conclusion. Here the disputed bridge is manufacture by humans, not the sediment date.

title: Precise snapshots may preclude repeated measurement
paragraphs: Resin casting gives precise models, but extracting them destroys the burrow; CT records both snapshots and construction over time.
B states no repeated castings of the same burrow. A/C invent size/time limits. D confuses destruction of burrow with distortion of cast.
transfer: Judge a method against the specific research goal. Accurate single-time measurement and longitudinal tracking are different capabilities.

title: A helpful result does not establish a helpful motive
paragraphs: Magpies peck another bird’s tracker off; Text1 suggests helping, while Text2 offers curiosity about novel equipment.
D permits adequate explanation without assisting intent. A relocates novelty to captivity, B invents acquiring tracker for self, C invents all-birds-participation criterion.
transfer: Separate what the action did from why the animal acted. An alternative motive can weaken an intentional reading without disproving the event.

title: Explain all observed features, not only the dominant one
paragraphs: Most sediment is fine mudstone from low-flow water, with desiccation cracks; some intervals are coarse sandstone from flowing water.
B combines long-lived lake, occasional drying, and stream periods. A denies lake; C reverses duration pattern; D assigns drying only to streams despite cracks in lake-associated grains.
transfer: Make one constraint per observation. A candidate must satisfy the complete list.

title: A second factor need not erase the first
paragraphs: Diet supplies flamingo pigments, but grooming moves stored pigments onto feathers.
C rejects shrimp quantity as the only determinant. A invents tail-versus-other-feather comparison. B invents imperceptibility; D invents seasonal diet.
transfer: “Also depends on” differs from “does not depend on.” Preserve the original mechanism while adding the missing factor.

title: Reconcile stipulated truths instead of rejecting one
paragraphs: Assume both thirteenth-century artifacts and fourteenth-century settlement founding are dated correctly.
B resolves both through earlier artifacts arriving by trade/migration. A inventories frequency without explaining dates, C invents prior founder-region assumption, D invents damage.
transfer: When the question explicitly grants two premises, hold both fixed and supply a compatible explanation.

title: Check the source explanation
paragraphs: Source text supports exploring molecules acting on Or31, which occurs in all known disease-carrying species. Rationale adds that Or31 may be uniquely shared, other receptor combinations are not shared by all species, single-receptor strategy is comparatively more effective, and mosquitoes will become resistant to EBF. These additions are not established by the passage. Teach shared-target relevance without those claims.

title: Check the source explanation
paragraphs: Passage says lighting has little effect on experienced cyclists; rationale shifts this to no effect and predicts their numbers stay the same. Key D is appropriately potential and novice-specific. Preserve little versus none; removing a deterrent supports potential rather than guaranteed increase.

title: Check the source explanation
paragraphs: Choice D says Sumerians were able to store extra crops. Rationale goes beyond ability to actual storage and says surplus must have been stored. Surplus supports the keyed opportunity, but alone does not establish exclusive disposition of extra crops.

title: Check the source explanation
paragraphs: Pure-umami versus mixed salty flavor makes D the best qualified inference in the supplied options. The rationale appeals to absence of soy sauce in the broths, but this alone is not a direct measurement of their dipeptide concentrations. Do not turn likely low amount into measured absence.

title: Check the source explanation
paragraphs: Parsed stem and rationale are empty because source headings are indented. Full raw record contains passage, all four choices, key B, and complete rationale; read directly. Agreement concerns fewer gestures despite one-versus-zero dispute.

title: Teaching scope correction
paragraphs: Ultimately can mark the underlying or highest-level goal, without a later event or final step. Bolívar addresses Cullen but ultimately seeks European political support.
transfer: Qualify final-step-only wording with an underlying-goal sense; use00221c00 as the contrast case.

title: Additional decision check
paragraphs: Carry negation, exceptions, and outlier labels into the proposition being linked. Apparent topic contrasts can elaborate a sentence that already says not always, prior assumptions differed, or outliers.
transfer: Before picking another contrast word, paraphrase the whole immediately preceding proposition, including its caveat. Existing relation categories alone do not make this explicit.

title: Additional decision check
paragraphs: A causal process described inside a sentence is not automatically a causal relationship between sentences. A mechanism can specify a broad causal claim; an eventual realization need not cause the state realized.
transfer: Separate event causation from evidence-to-inference and general-claim-to-mechanism links. Ask exactly what the earlier proposition would be claimed to cause.

title: Source rationale precision
paragraphs: Official rationale calls microscope visibility an exception to earlier crystalline invisibility, but the immediate preceding microcrystalline statement concerns naked-eye invisibility. The full context contrasts cryptocrystalline and microcrystalline microscope behavior.
transfer: Explain that said as a limitation/contrast between visibility conditions and mineral classes; avoid claiming the sentence logically contradicts naked-eye invisibility.

title: Additional decision check
paragraphs: Nested supplements require identifying punctuation levels: Calle uses outer dashes enclosing two linked supplements separated by a comma; Anderson uses a trailing decision appositive whose relative clause contains its own comma-bounded by allowing phrase. Existing single-aside rules apply but do not explicitly show this combination.
transfer: Add one nested-supplement walkthrough: remove the entire outer supplement first, then pair any punctuation inside it. Do not pair an inner comma with an outer dash or mistake that, by...own, amplified for a clause boundary.

title: Additional decision check
paragraphs: Singular agreement alone does not choose it versus this/that. The source chooses it to resume a given term and a hypothetical object, rejecting singular this/that for ambiguity or inappropriate specific pointing, while this is correct for an entire appointment event. Existing uses show both outcomes but do not explicitly compare their reference jobs.
transfer: After checking number, identify whether the blank resumes a noun or points to an entire event/proposition. Explain why a matching-number demonstrative can still leave the intended referent unclear; do not teach an absolute prohibition on demonstratives with noun antecedents.

title: Source rationale precision
paragraphs: Official rationale correctly selects finite have used but labels it past perfect. Have used is present perfect; past perfect would be had used. The item tests finite verb supply, so the answer remains sound.
transfer: When explaining this source, call have used a finite present-perfect verb phrase; do not carry over the source’s incorrect tense label.

title: Source punctuation discrepancy
paragraphs: PDF p1966 confirms official D swimming, and rationale explicitly says comma after swimming pairs with dash after ciliates. However, the text has an inner dash before including and closing dash before bestows, leaving the outer widely understood participial supplement without its expected closing comma. This source anomaly conflicts with the same-mark aside rules elsewhere. Finite alternatives remain wrong because bestows is the main predicate.
transfer: Preserve official answer but annotate source punctuation as anomalous. Use clean 1a61e2ae as the printed-participle version’s teaching example, or transparently label any normalized punctuation. Do not teach comma–dash pairing as a general exception inferred from this item.

title: Weakening an identification does not identify its rival
paragraphs: B makes both jellyfish and ctenophore identification inconclusive. That weakens the claimed ctenophore identity without proving jellyfish. A comparative preservation advantage alone (D) does not establish inability to identify.

title: Test the exact relationship, not a nearby topic
paragraphs: Art–reality relationships differ when one theory permits hypothetical realities not already existing. Shared audience psychology or word history does not answer the translation claim.

title: An adaptation explanation needs a trait-specific resource advantage
paragraphs: Different available prey alone does not explain smaller size. Access to shallow foraging areas inaccessible to larger whales supplies the missing size-to-benefit mechanism.

title: Normalized baseline and significance are separate from bar height
paragraphs: Graph axis notes differences from baseline were not statistically significant. A visual bar above 100% does not establish significant rebound. Source rationale’s “all seals” and “prolonged period” expectations are stronger than the definition supplied; retain the tentative “may not” conclusion and keyed A.

title: Marine reptiles become mammals in one rationale sentence
paragraphs: Correct-answer rationale says “nonendothermic marine mammals” where passage and C say marine reptiles. This is a noun slip; key C remains supported.

title: B states the result but omits the study
paragraphs: Source rejection says B “doesn’t include the study’s findings” despite B giving 74 Orchidaceae species. The supported reason is its failure to present the study. A supplies study attribution and result; key unchanged.

title: Emphasis depends on sentence structure, not fact presence
paragraphs: B mentions different topics but ends on shared influence; A concedes shared effect before foregrounding autobiography versus fiction. For an emphasis goal, merely containing a true difference is insufficient.

title: Historical context requires the claim plus its intellectual setting
paragraphs: A links Einstein’s independent reality claim to the field’s emergence and subsequent acceptance of the rival view. A date or famous debate alone does not give the requested argument in context.

title: Cross-check every requested outcome against the same focal group
paragraphs: D compares positive versus both controls for enjoyment and endurance. A’s endurance comparison leaves positive feedback out, so cannot establish absence of its physical effect.

title: Carrying capacity counts individuals of one species
paragraphs: C says maximum number of species, conflicting with notes’ maximum number of a species. Rationale calls C a definition and rejects only lack of wolf count. Correct instruction: C also misdefines carrying capacity. D remains correct.

title: Challenging priority does not deny accomplishment
paragraphs: Earlier Indigenous fossil discovery would challenge Plot’s being first, not his having found dinosaur remains. Also preserve scope: general dinosaur priority is not priority for M. carinatus specifically.

title: Track the actor and material through a process
paragraphs: A/B/D use process vocabulary but change what passes the dead zone, what is baked, or when curing ends. C preserves UV→resin layers→object oven sequence.

title: The goal determines which source details belong in a narrative opening
paragraphs: Prompt calls VGHS award-nominated to identify its subject, but the requested opening is best served by protagonist, named series, genre, and launch time. A need not repeat the award; outcome-only B jumps past introduction.

title: Stellar mass is not radius
paragraphs: D correctly says SiriusA is more massive than Sun. Source rationale glosses this as larger; retain mass terminology because the notes’ solar masses do not establish radius.

title: Quoted wording must remain exact
paragraphs: D changes notes’ quoted “unsung heroines of the Ghanaian Republic” to “unsung heroes of the Ghanaian Republic.” Source rejection only addresses wrong purpose. It also inaccurately quotes the notes. A remains correct.

title: A concessive clause may contain the requested fact without emphasizing it
paragraphs: D concedes discovery significance with “Though” then foregrounds erroneous hypothesis. A foregrounds significance and consequences; importance merely appearing is not enough.

title: Match the exact comparison axis
paragraphs: Goal asks how GREEN backgrounds are used across countries. A contrasts colors on highways; B holds color fixed and contrasts the road classes receiving it. A true contrast can still answer a nearby question.

title: A valid contrast can use a secondary measured characteristic
paragraphs: D contrasts sample thicknesses rather than main temperature-change results. Broad “contrast samples” goal allows this supported difference; avoid imposing a more specific goal absent from question.

title: Promising potential is not established commercial viability
paragraphs: A reuses quoted words “commercially viable” but changes authors’ conclusion from “promising potential as a commercially viable” crop to marigolds WERE commercially viable. Source rationale only rejects incompleteness. A also overstates conclusion strength. C remains correct.

title: A shared failure can arise from different failed criteria
paragraphs: A groups CTAB2X and Pplant as less effective because each fails at least one of yield/purity. They need not have the same failed metric or matching numerical values. The goal is the significance of their shared inability to meet both criteria.

title: Syllables per second do not measure information per second
paragraphs: B claims information is conveyed faster in Spanish based on 7.7 versus5.3 syllables/sec, though notes distinguish roughly constant information rates from varying syllable rates. Rationale rejects only limited overview; B also conflates metrics. D remains correct.

title: Explain a change with a changing mechanism
paragraphs: D gives current closeness and apparent merging; C specifically says stars moved together since older accounts. To explain appearance change, preserve the temporal movement rather than static condition alone.

title: Choose the requested event sequence, not the investigators’ workflow
paragraphs: D gives proposal→simulation→hypothesis sequence. C gives the physical history proposed in the study, which is the requested target. Same sequence vocabulary can describe the wrong events.

title: A statistic stays attached to its measured outcome and causal direction
paragraphs: D changes99% less hunting time caused by more tuna into99% tuna increase caused by changed hunting. Both the metric and causal arrow must survive synthesis. B also upgrades pending deterrent testing to proven efficacy.

title: At most25% includes sites meeting zero needs
paragraphs: C’s first clause is consistent with the graph:0% and up-to25% sites together exceed80% currently. Its second clause fails because the maximum-temperature >25% bar is about78%, below80%. Source rationale rejects C by listing0% and up-to25% separately without identifying the false second clause. Key D remains correct.

title: Peeling benefit is an answer-choice detail, not a premise
paragraphs: Source rejection of D says Armijo’s hypothesis mentions easier peeling, but the passage only hypothesizes reduced roasting time from more heliostats. Easier peeling appears only in distractor D. Reject D because it measures the wrong outcome; key B remains correct.

title: An indirect effect needs both directional links
paragraphs: B supplies NFM→lower political knowledge/interest and knowledge/interest→higher voting likelihood. Combining those signs supports reduced voting likelihood indirectly; identifying a mediator alone or mentioning network size without directional first link is insufficient. The passage keeps this as may reduce rather than a direct voting experiment.

title: Explain a cost gap with a difference in effects
paragraphs: C links more frequent replacement to repeated higher new-material costs, explaining a widening new-versus-recycled cost gap. B foregrounds rising cumulative costs, which could affect both groups; its concession about potential recycling savings does not draw the needed comparative conclusion. Track total levels separately from the gap between them.

title: Bar differences do not establish statistical significance
paragraphs: Source describes significantly lower metal levels, but graph supplies heights without uncertainty or a test. D describes lower levels and remains supported; avoid statistical-significance claims.

title: Recall decay needs a comparison group
paragraphs: D says sharers forget details after a week; without low-engagement recall at that delay this does not establish weaker relative recall. C directly compares comments and links and remains correct.

title: A cross-species comparison does not test fungal benefit
paragraphs: B compares corn with broccoli in fungal soil. Its rationale instead discusses corn being more massive with fungi, a within-species comparison B never makes. Reject B because species differ independently of treatment; A remains correct.

title: Highest spray efficiency is near17%, not14–16%
paragraphs: Graph places highest spray coating near17%, above16%; source rejection of C incorrectly gives14–16% for that highest bar. Lowest spray~15.5% still exceeds best spin~13.5%, so B remains correct.

title: Algeria exceeds70% in2020
paragraphs: Graph places Algeria near75% in2020. Source repeatedly says reached70%; choice D correctly says more than70%. Preserve the distinction when teaching threshold readings.

title: A trend distractor can also misstate a value
paragraphs: D claims both lakes exceed105days in2005–06; Neusiedl is about100–102, below105. Source rejection only notes the missing before/after comparison and says graph could indicate the claim. C remains correct.

title: All thrum genera change; the direction differs
paragraphs: Source says intact/damaged thrum time differs for only some genera. Table shows differences for all four: Habropoda4.1→9.5,Osmia7.1→8.3,Pierid2.4→1.9,Xylocopa2.5→2.2. A correctly distinguishes increases from decreases; do not equate decreasing with no effect.

title: A force-to-weight claim needs the denominator ratio
paragraphs: The relevant support is that weight ratio is close to1 while force ratio exceeds4. Merely both weighing above450g cannot constrain their ratio. Graph also shows~510and490g rather than source approximation500and480g; keyD unchanged.

title: Reject the choice actually printed
paragraphs: A dates the Fairfield Gorget to the earlier Woodland period; its source rejection instead discusses a Mexican artifact appearing only after the gorget. That artifact is absent from A. A supplies no Mexican-art contact evidence, whereas C supplies a nearby contemporaneous Mexican object. Key C remains supported; PDF page visually checked.

title: A cross-year comparison does not contradict a same-year treatment effect
paragraphs: C accurately compares 2018 control yield with 2019 nitrogen yield. The rationale calls this a strong conflict with nitrogen improving yield, but weather or other year effects can coexist with nitrogen outperforming same-year controls in every year. Reject C because it does not isolate the treatment comparison; retain B. Graph and source rationale card visually checked.

title: Borrowed vocabulary does not establish related language families
paragraphs: The rationale says Caddo is described as closely related to the Totozoquean family. The passage actually proposes cultural contact and borrowing of corn vocabulary through unrelated Chitimacha. A is supported by corn cultivation without demonstrably Totozoquean-derived corn words in Cherokee/Muskogean; do not turn lexical borrowing into a genealogical language relationship. PDF page visually checked.

title: Share of authors differs from share of works
paragraphs: A reports the percentage of Random House AUTHORS who were Black. Its correct-answer rationale paraphrases that as a higher percentage of WORKS by Black authors. Authors can publish different numbers of works, so those denominators are not interchangeable. The author-share increase itself supports the likely representation aim; key A remains supported.

title: Test necessity and insufficiency with two different observations
paragraphs: In the displayed sample every total-outlay decrease occurs during divided Congress, while the divided 1975–1976 period has an increase of 2.7 percentage points. The first pattern supports necessity in this sample; the exception shows division is insufficient. Component defense/nondefense decreases cannot substitute for total outlays. D remains correct; source table visually checked.

title: A knockout label names what is absent
paragraphs: Type A means DptA is silenced and DptB remains active. Its high survival after A. sicerae infection therefore supports a role for DptB, while low survival of B and AB tracks DptB absence. No both-active group is graphed, and only two pathogens are discussed, so do not infer the both-active optimum or universal pathogen exclusivity. C remains correct; source graph visually checked.

title: Use a global upper bound to constrain a local subgroup
paragraphs: Tanzania has 61 million Swahili speakers, while at most 15 million worldwide have Swahili as a first language. Even assigning every first-language speaker to Tanzania leaves at least roughly 46 million later-language speakers there. The proof does not require knowing how native speakers are distributed among countries. A remains correct; source table visually checked.

title: Assigned retrieval condition does not necessarily equal the original source of knowledge.
paragraphs: Participants instructed to look up an answer might already know it. Their subsequent attribution to memory can be accurate, so the useful validity question separates prior knowledge from smartphone-induced source confusion. Correct D addresses this alternative; confidence, correctness and an equal delay do not.
transfer: Add an evaluation branch for questions about validity: identify what the operational measure labels as an error, then test whether it can occur without the hypothesized process.

title: Variable costs can still be independent of donation size.
paragraphs: Costs vary across donors but do not rise with donation amount. Fewer large gifts reduce the number of reimbursements for a target total. Independent of fits; supplemental, predictive and subsumed do not explain the preference.
transfer: For relational vocabulary, name both variables and preserve which relationship is absent; do not replace independent with fixed.

title: Comprehensiveness of testimony and coherence of authorial viewpoint are separate qualities.
paragraphs: The oral history is valuable and broad, yet lacks an authorial voice that unifies accounts. Its limitation does not imply omitted events or low participation.
transfer: When summarizing a qualified evaluation, name the specific limitation before reading choices that substitute a different defect.

title: An exception to a behavioral trend can confirm the same explanatory framework.
paragraphs: Moonlight inhibits most nocturnal mammals but promotes mongoose lemur activity. Both outcomes are explained by risk-reward balance; visually dependent lemurs receive a different foraging benefit. Correct B accounts for both, whereas D wrongly says the exception undermines the explanation.
transfer: In structure answers, ask whether the exception violates the proposed mechanism or reflects different inputs to that mechanism.

title: A defining vocabulary clue can occur in the following sentence, outside the blank’s own sentence.
paragraphs: The first sentence supplies no explanation of how the diaphragm contracts; the following sentence calls the contractions uncontrollable, which directly supports involuntarily. Beneficial infant effects are a separate qualified claim.
transfer: Start at the target sentence but read neighboring sentences for repeated referents and definitions before deciding that the clue is missing.

title: An unreal alternative within the same event is counterfactual, rather than a replay of the past or an analogy to another context.
paragraphs: Viewers look where the ball would have traveled had its actual collider been absent. Counterfactual names that contrary-to-fact scenario; retrospective would revisit what happened, and analogical would compare a different but comparable context.
transfer: For mental-scenario vocabulary, identify whether the imagined event actually happened, alters an element of the same event, or transfers its structure to another setting.

title: Research–event disagreement can arise from strategic timing within real-world observations, without invalidating the data as unreal or inconsistent.
paragraphs: Earlier election data mostly concern governments that postponed austerity until after voting; recent cases did not. The opening discrepancy is explained by this complicating circumstance, not by laboratory data, competing research groups, or researchers ignoring inconsistent records.
transfer: When a function answer includes the later explanation, paraphrase the exact data-generating circumstance and reject substitutions that change it into researcher error or a laboratory-versus-reality split.

title: Check the source explanation
paragraphs: Correct B is secure from pronunciation help and classes. Rationale for D says that if she were delighted to speak the language there would be no challenge; enthusiasm can coexist with limited skill. D fails because it does not express the obstacle required by but and this challenge, not because excitement eliminates difficulty.

title: Check the source explanation
paragraphs: The text distinguishes obligately migrating diadromous fish from those merely tolerant of salinity. The rationale generalizes that euryhaline fish do not relocate; salinity tolerance alone does not rule out migration. Key A rests on obligate migration versus tolerance without that requirement.

title: Check the source explanation
paragraphs: Opaque securely means unclear about data practices. The rationale defines this as deliberately avoiding clear information, but the passage establishes lack of clarity and advocates’ response without proving intentional concealment.
